items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (first day of early voting; reports published ~7-8 PM PDT Oct 13)
items.summary: The Georgia Secretary of State's Office reported more than 170,000 ballots cast on the first day of early voting, Tuesday Oct 13 — calling it a midterm early-voting turnout record. Atlanta journalist King Williams, citing VoteHub data, put the full-day figure at a record 188,628, the highest first-day turnout ever for a Georgia midterm (+28% vs 2022); Fulton County led turnout and Chatham County topped 1,000 ballots in the first six hours. Early in-person voting continues through Oct 30.
items.title: Georgia sets midterm early-voting record on first day: 170,000+ ballots cast

items.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday, Oct 13 declined to hear an appeal from Andrew Parker and his firm over the $122,000 in sanctions imposed by U.S. District Judge John Tuchi for 'baseless' claims in the Kari Lake/Mark Finchem lawsuit that sought to ban electronic tabulators in Arizona's 2022 midterms and require hand counts. The 9th Circuit had upheld the sanctions; they apply to the lawyers, not to Lake or Finchem. With the high court declining review, the sanctions are final — a signal that courts will keep punishing unfounded election-fraud litigation ahead of the 2026 midterms.
items.title: SCOTUS lets $122K sanctions stand on lawyers behind Lake/Finchem 2022 voting-machine suit
